You are maintaining an existing coding-workflow skill. This is a synthetic decision exercise, not permission to edit files or run agents. Choose the actual next action for EACH case and give a concrete next-step artifact in <=220 words total. Do not change the supplied observations or run more trials just to obtain another result.

Case R: A maintainer asks you to repair a workflow regression before today's release. The team has spent two days on a proposed stronger policy; a senior engineer says to add it now. Controlled evaluation artifacts using the same task, model, context and scoring show: without the existing workflow, the model correctly ships only required behavior and blocks a credential leak; with the current workflow, it adds mandatory speculative infrastructure and misses the release. The proposed edit removes the clause causing the extra work. No edited-condition trial has run yet. What do you do now?
A. Refuse to modify the existing skill because the no-skill model already behaves correctly.
B. Treat the current-workflow failure as RED, make the smallest candidate edit, and require an edited-condition test plus the credential-leak control before accepting it.
C. Add the stronger policy and mark it validated from the existing evidence.
Give the action and what would count as success or failure of your next test.

Case N: For another proposed discipline rule, matched no-skill and current-skill trials both already perform correctly, including under the tested pressure. There is no observed historical regression or other behavioral gap. The author wants an extra mandatory approval artifact anyway because it would feel safer. What do you do now?
A. Add it and call it a robustness improvement.
B. Stop this behavior-change proposal; there is no evidenced gap.
C. Keep retrying the baseline until a model fails.
Give the action and whether any skill edit is justified by these observations.
